technical_validation.duplicate_guard_evidence: r4 checkpoint/rebuild paths reject duplicate ownership; current registry read found one owner per frozen target.
technical_validation.qualification: Mutable global registry was read only for ownership and not hash-locked.

items.evidence: Paragraph 56 illustrates agency plagiarism, intent and credibility findings about another candidate.
items.scope_review: The next paragraph's judicial confirmation is outside the target; this is neither applicant guilt nor a standalone current-court fraud test.

items.evidence: Paragraph 110 separately requires Commission satisfaction, not mere reasonable grounds, for a post-investigation section 69 order and attributes the civil balance-of-probabilities candidate-fraud standard to a cited Court.
items.scope_review: Qualification: the two speakers and stages must remain distinct. The threshold AU concerns an order following investigation; the proof AU concerns an investigator determining candidate fraud. Their primary spans are disjoint.

items.evidence: Paragraph 9 identifies allegations outside this application and explains how the investigation began.
items.scope_review: It adjudicates neither the other persons' allegations nor any immunity for this applicant.

items.evidence: Paragraph 24 states Rule 303(3) substitution on Attorney General motion when the Court is satisfied of inability or unwillingness after naming under Rule 303(2).
items.scope_review: Qualification: substitution is permissive and conditional, not automatic. The no-motion fact in this case is separate from the rule.

items.evidence: Paragraph 108 separately states notice/relevant-document access for a summoned interviewee and, if applicable, ability to invoke Canada Evidence Act section 5 protection.
items.scope_review: Qualification: relevant-document, summoned-person and if-applicable limits are essential. The Charter section 13 statement is tentative (`no longer seems really necessary`) and creates no blanket right to refuse questions. The primary spans are adjacent and non-overlapping.

items.evidence: Paragraph 93 declines a definitive jurisdiction/reasonableness opinion and refuses to base allowance on that contentious issue.
items.scope_review: Qualification: the preceding inclination to agree with the applicant is not a final lack-of-jurisdiction holding. Procedural fairness, not jurisdiction merits, is determinative here.

items.evidence: Paragraph 103 states subsection 70(2)'s informal/expeditious procedure and retained Part II Inquiries Act commissioner powers.
items.scope_review: Qualification: procedural flexibility and broad inquiry powers do not exempt the Commission from fairness obligations discussed in the surrounding analysis.

items.evidence: Paragraph 169 identifies as determinative the final report approval without applicant comment on final fraud conclusions and analysis.
items.scope_review: Qualification: this is an alleged-fraud, case-specific omission. It does not announce that every administrative draft in every process must be disclosed.

items.evidence: Paragraph 98 says section 72 legislatively recognizes submissions when a person's appointment or proposed appointment is at issue.
items.scope_review: Qualification: the appointment-at-issue condition is indispensable. The provision is not stated as a general submissions entitlement for every investigation or third-party sanction.

items.evidence: Paragraph 158 recounts a revised factual-report comment request, deadline and perceived transition to analysis/conclusions.
items.scope_review: It establishes neither a generally lawful deadline nor that factual-report comments cured nondisclosure of final analysis.

boundaries.note: Only frozen fourteenth10 decisions are accepted; mutable overall progress is outside scope.
